instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: Formatter execution, trigger timing, configuration, and evidence ownership are explicitly centralized in this document, with anchor-based consumption required elsewhere.
atoms.title: Canonical formatter ownership is explicit

atoms.statement: A formatter is a stateless external in-place transform triggered only after a successful write, edit, patch, or multiedit event carrying path and extension.
atoms.title: Formatter and trigger semantics are defined

atoms.statement: The trigger declares only path and extension and calls itself merely equivalent to `File.Edited`; it does not define the exact event type/version, event or operation identifier, project identity, ordering guarantees, replay/idempotency rule, or canonical producer/consumer registration.
atoms.title: Trigger event envelope and ordering are unspecified

atoms.statement: Ownership is delegated to Plugins_System and FileSafe, but this formatter contract does not define the mandatory handoff data, denial behavior, or enforcement point connecting formatter dispatch to subprocess and file-safety authorization.
atoms.title: Safety-owner handoff lacks an executable contract

atoms.statement: HTE writes resolve enabled extension matches and execute them sequentially, while DAE delegates formatting entirely to provider CLIs.
atoms.title: HTE lifecycle and DAE exclusion are explicit

atoms.statement: Sequential execution is specified only within a formatter chain; there is no per-file serialization, revision precondition, stale-write detection, chain snapshot, or rule for a second hosted edit arriving while the first chain runs.
atoms.title: Concurrent edits can race formatter chains

atoms.statement: The lifecycle records `format.applied` only for changes beyond whitespace, while AC-FMT06 requires evidence for formatting changes without that exception.
atoms.title: Whitespace-only evidence rule contradicts AC-FMT06

atoms.statement: Original-output preservation is required but the plan never defines temp-copy execution, fsync/rename boundaries, backup lifetime, restore failure handling, or what later formatters see after one formatter fails.
atoms.title: Non-zero exit recovery is asserted but not made atomic

atoms.statement: The built-in catalog is extension- and detector-specific and enables entries by default after a successful session or project-switch check.
atoms.title: Built-in formatter catalog is concretely enumerated

atoms.statement: Detection runs once per session or project switch, but cache key, invalidation, manual refresh, PATH/config changes, detector timeout, and failed-check observability are not defined.
atoms.title: Built-in detection freshness is unspecified

atoms.statement: The command/environment schema does not define direct argv execution versus shell interpretation, environment inheritance and denylisting, working directory, executable trust, user consent, timeout/cancellation, process-tree termination, or stdout/stderr byte limits.
atoms.title: Formatter subprocess execution lacks minimum security controls

atoms.statement: Absolute-path substitution is deterministic, but path canonicalization, symlink policy, allowed roots, special-file rejection, authorization timing, and time-of-check/time-of-use revalidation are not defined here.
atoms.title: `$FILE` targeting omits FileSafe validation semantics

atoms.statement: Custom formatters are always enabled absent `disabled = true`, but ID grammar, normalization, built-in collision behavior, duplicate handling across scopes, provenance display, and first-run approval are unspecified.
atoms.title: Custom formatter identity and trust states are incomplete

atoms.statement: Project config overrides global per formatter, but field-level versus object-level merge, missing/null/empty semantics, environment-map merge, global-kill-switch precedence, deletion/tombstone behavior, and invalid-layer recovery are not specified.
atoms.title: Global/project formatter merge is not deterministic

atoms.statement: The Settings tab exposes global and per-formatter controls, statuses, detail editors, add/remove workflows, validation, and scope selection.
atoms.title: Formatter Settings control inventory is explicit

atoms.statement: The add/remove/edit surface lacks save timing, dirty-state behavior, scope-switch handling, write-conflict behavior, inline validation copy, persistence failure recovery, destructive confirmation/undo, and post-save success/error truth.
atoms.title: Formatter GUI mutations lack save and recovery states

atoms.statement: The mode split and tooltip prefix are defined, but keyboard/table semantics, screen-reader names, focus after expansion/removal, localization keys for labels/status/errors, truncation disclosure, and ELI5 visibility of active Expert configuration are not.
atoms.title: Interaction modes omit accessibility and localization oracles

atoms.statement: The OpenCode baseline captures event triggering, detection, disable/config shape, placeholder behavior, and custom formatter support.
atoms.title: External formatter baseline is retained

atoms.statement: Puppet Master intentionally diverges from OpenCode through Rust event dispatch, Rust-side executable resolution, evidence recording, and HTE-only enforcement.

atoms.statement: The event examples enumerate selected metadata but do not define a complete registered schema, required EventRecord fields, operation/run correlation, before/after hashes, whitespace classification, redaction/truncation for stderr, or per-chain sequence.

atoms.statement: A dedicated editable Formatter Settings GUI is an intentional Puppet Master product delta.
atoms.title: GUI formatter configuration is an explicit delta

atoms.statement: The config-editing delta does not define secret-value masking/storage/redaction, inherited-versus-explicit environment display, status provenance or freshness, last detection error, or the distinction between configured, detected, enabled, and runnable.

atoms.statement: FS-001 is explicitly retired to migration lineage, while FS-002 through FS-015 own product behavior and GUI coverage.

atoms.statement: GRS-015 defines progress fingerprints, blocker signatures, repeated-no-progress detection, hard budget fields, distinct limit statuses, deterministic validators, and repair/adjudication routing for identical blockers.

atoms.statement: GRS-015 sets max_parallel_agents=0 by default and says a parent or user policy may narrow defaults, while GRS-016 prefers subagents by default and requires parallel spawning to honor that cap. Zero is not defined as auto/unbounded, and narrowing zero cannot enable agents.

atoms.statement: The required defaults set max_tokens to null and delegate a concrete ceiling to provider/model policy, but do not require that resolution to succeed or define a blocked state when no provider ceiling exists.

atoms.statement: GRS-016 requires child identity, scope, budgets, recovery and receipts, bounds parallelism and write conflict, and reserves synthesis, merge, verification, and parent completion to the parent.

atoms.statement: GRS-017 defaults child work to read-only/proposal-only and requires a worktree, explicit non-overlap, or a parent-granted single-writer lease before direct mutation.

atoms.statement: GRS-018 catalogs goal classes and gives concrete oracles for bug fix, feature build, test-until-pass, doc update, and ledger-to-plan transfer while retaining the no-WorkNode boundary.

atoms.statement: The canonical text promises criteria for every template, but repo_research, refactor, migration, and governance seal have no concrete completion criteria in the PlanUnit or its acceptance list; audit_and_repair is named in the list but also lacks a direct criterion here.

atoms.statement: GRS-019 supplies autonomous recovery actions and requires blocked state to carry cause, scope, prior recovery, safety stop reason, and next safe action rather than a generic failure.

atoms.statement: GRS-031 allows visible launch/provisioning progress but explicitly withholds running status and runnable WorkNodes until atomic activation commits with a durable start receipt.

atoms.statement: MGAC-015 and MGAC-016 define a single envelope that returns output or error for image, video, TTS, and music, but specify no queued/running/polling/cancelled/timed-out/partially-persisted states, progress events, reconnect behavior, or restart recovery.
atoms.title: Long-running media has no explicit attempt state machine

atoms.statement: MGAC-016 enumerates a closed-looking field set with no input artifact/image references, mask, source media, custom width/height, provider option namespace, safety/moderation control, callback/polling handle, or forward-compatible extensions object.
atoms.title: Common request envelope cannot express editing inputs or provider extensions

atoms.statement: MGAC-017 declares last-match-wins and cross-family authority while MGAC-018 declares alias-first model resolution, but neither PlanUnit defines duplicate controls across body/block, alias shadowing, normalized-name collisions, integer overflow, unsupported route dimensions, or executable vectors for these boundaries.
atoms.title: Normalization and model resolution lack collision and boundary oracles

atoms.statement: MGAC-019 explicitly refuses to infer generated-image output from Cursor image-input/API-key evidence and uses BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED or a route-specific unavailable state for unsupported kinds.
atoms.title: Cursor generated output requires route-level proof

atoms.statement: MGAC-020 and MGAC-023 replace Gemini-default shorthand with concrete route taxonomy and explicitly prohibit active Gemini CLI media, Nanobanana installation, NANOBANANA_API_KEY injection, and undisclosed fallback.
atoms.title: Retired Gemini CLI and Nanobanana routes are dispositioned clearly

atoms.statement: MGAC-021 correctly imports quota, usage, and account/plan UI labels from Multi-Account and usage-feature instead of creating a media-local accounting or identity bucket.
atoms.title: Media account and usage labels consume owner truth

atoms.statement: MGAC-022 and MGAC-024 name shared runtime, usage, storage, receipt, redb, and event-sourced owners but do not bind concrete schema IDs, field paths, key cardinalities, projection freshness, receipt linkage, or migration rules; their preserved ContractRefs do not even name the storage and usage owners emphasized in canonical text.
atoms.title: Shared runtime and storage authority boundaries are prose-only

atoms.statement: MGAC-025 mandates project, lane, worktree, thread, request, runtime, usage, route, artifact, and recovery identity but gives no envelope schema, requiredness, uniqueness scope, parent/attempt relationships, target/account separation representation, or cardinality for multi-project execution.
atoms.title: Concurrent media identity and common envelope remain under-specified

atoms.statement: All six accepted units retain empty dependencies/unblocks and generic source-preservation acceptance criteria despite relying on shared runtime, account, usage, storage, receipt, orchestration, and GUI owners and despite several being marked split-recommended.
atoms.title: MGAC-020 through MGAC-025 are not readiness-grade PlanUnits

atoms.statement: The assigned units define successful and failed media.generate envelopes, deterministic artifact manifests and write ordering, supersession visibility, isolated concurrent request directories, route-specific Cursor failures, and a stable nine-code error vocabulary.
atoms.title: Media generation response, persistence, concurrency, and failure contracts

atoms.statement: The artifact rules require files before manifest and prohibit a false success manifest, but do not define atomic manifest publication, cleanup or tombstone behavior for orphaned files, crash recovery scanning, or how supersession and retry races are serialized.
atoms.title: Crash-consistent artifact recovery is not fully specified

atoms.statement: The assigned units establish raw and normalized prompt copies, trailing controls detection and parse-first ordering, tolerance of malformed controls, exact bounded controls and token-gate regexes, and highest-priority prefix kind detection.
atoms.title: Deterministic prompt preprocessing and kind-detection boundary

atoms.statement: The deterministic mini grammar fixes ASCII-oriented regex vocabulary and a 400-character controls capture, but does not define Unicode normalization, locale-sensitive lowercasing, multiline limits, regex time or memory budgets, or deterministic handling of mixed-script and conflicting kind tokens.
atoms.title: Unicode, locale, and regex resource behavior are unspecified

atoms.statement: The assigned units define keyword kind families, an ambiguity gate for verb fallback, controls-over-all precedence, an exact slot order, model candidate extraction and resolution, count clamping with last-match wins, and numeric or named aspect mapping.
atoms.title: Kind, precedence, model, count, and aspect extraction rules

atoms.statement: The units specify precedence and selected happy-path mappings but do not define outcomes for zero or negative counts, zero-dimension or extreme numeric aspect ratios, duplicate conflicting controls, multiple model candidates, normalization collisions, or conflicts between last-match-wins and controls-over-all precedence.
atoms.title: Invalid and conflicting extracted values lack a complete decision table

atoms.statement: The assigned units define size and resolution candidates and kind guards, video or music duration extraction, canonical output formats, TTS voice extraction, guarded quality candidates, and bounded digit seed extraction.
atoms.title: Media slot candidate extraction and guarded assignment

atoms.statement: Candidate extraction does not define canonical validation or failure behavior for unsupported kind-format pairs, provider-specific size and duration limits, invalid voice IDs, seed overflow after parsing, mutually incompatible resolution fields, or whether unavailable values fail, clamp, or fall back.
atoms.title: Provider validation, numeric ranges, and unsupported combinations are unresolved

atoms.statement: The assigned units define BPM and negative-prompt extraction, order-preserving dedupe, conservative prompt cleanup, four mapped picker rows, accessible disabled presentation, route-specific setup footer copy, and single pinned shared-footer behavior.
atoms.title: Final prompt cleanup and accessible capability-picker presentation

atoms.statement: The picker contracts do not define focus retention, active-descendant behavior, scroll anchoring, live-region announcement, tooltip dismissal, or footer-link behavior when capability eligibility changes while the list is open or while keyboard navigation is active.
atoms.title: Open-picker state changes lack interaction and accessibility oracles

atoms.statement: The assigned units bind generated-media availability to verified routes, insert canonical per-capability prompts, scope inline model overrides to one request, refresh picker state without clearing composer text, define disabled-reason copy, and require capabilities.get to expose media and registered provider-tool capabilities.
atoms.title: Backend capability truth, picker actions, refresh, copy, and return-shape oracle

atoms.statement: The refresh rule does not define event ordering, debounce or coalescing, revision identity, cancellation, stale capabilities.get response suppression, offline transition behavior, or what happens when a user clicks an item whose route is revoked during refresh.
atoms.title: Capability refresh ordering and stale-result suppression are unspecified

atoms.statement: The assigned units assert disabled-reason enum integrity, route-gated Cursor behavior, disclosed provider switching, provider/model media-kind eligibility, missing-route disablement, one-request model override resolution, and disabled picker display.
atoms.title: Media acceptance criteria for enums, routing, overrides, and picker display

atoms.statement: MGAC-068 requires disabled_reason to use exactly six canonical values with no ad-hoc strings, while MGAC-072 permits UNSUPPORTED, CAPABILITY_GATED, or a more specific provider/account state; those values are not among the six named by the assigned disabled-reason copy contract.
atoms.title: Missing-route states contradict the six-value disabled_reason contract

atoms.statement: Clicking an enabled picker capability inserts the section 5.1 prompt verbatim into the chat composer.
atoms.title: Capability click inserts canonical prompt

atoms.statement: Assistant and Interviewer flows, including PRD Builder, must resolve capability questions through capabilities.get.
atoms.title: Capability lookup callers are named

atoms.statement: Other plan documents must consume media rules by anchor rather than duplicate them.
atoms.title: DRY anchor authority is explicit

atoms.statement: Turning the Media setting off maps an otherwise available capability to disabled with ADMIN_DISABLED.
atoms.title: Admin toggle disablement is deterministic

atoms.statement: Infrastructure disablement outranks ADMIN_DISABLED when multiple disable reasons apply.
atoms.title: Disable-reason precedence is fixed

atoms.statement: Explicit non-Cursor provider, route, and auth selections prohibit silent cross-fallback.
atoms.title: Media route fallback respects user authority

atoms.statement: Media availability, usage, quota, and account-plan disclosure remain route-specific and exclude retired route rows.
atoms.title: Route-specific media disclosure avoids stale mixed state

atoms.statement: Successful media responses use persisted artifacts plus manifest metadata and forbid inline data_uri transport.
atoms.title: Generated media responses are artifact-backed

atoms.statement: media.generate failures are limited to the nine canonical section 2.6 error codes.
atoms.title: Media failures use a closed stable enum

atoms.statement: capabilities.get evaluates the current runtime registry snapshot at each call and must not return stale enablement.
atoms.title: Capability evaluation is call-time current

atoms.statement: Artifact bytes must become durable before manifest publication, including partial-failure handling.
atoms.title: Artifact-before-manifest durability is explicit

atoms.statement: The picker exposes disabled items and reasons accessibly, pins configuration recovery, and refreshes without clearing composer text.
atoms.title: Picker accessibility and refresh behavior are bound

atoms.statement: Appendix A mirrors deterministic slot rules 1 through 7 but is explicitly barred from becoming a second behavioral owner.
atoms.title: Slot-rule mirror preserves single ownership

atoms.statement: Appendix A mirrors duration, format, and TTS voice extraction while ownership remains with MGAC-049 through MGAC-051.
atoms.title: Duration, format, and voice extraction are mirrored

atoms.statement: Quality parsing is context-gated, while seed and BPM use explicit numeric patterns.
atoms.title: Quality extraction rejects creative-adjective false positives

atoms.statement: Negative prompt extraction combines explicit text and all avoid clauses with order-preserving deduplication.
atoms.title: Negative-prompt combination is deterministic

atoms.statement: Prompt cleaning says to remove matched control spans and preserve creative text, but does not define overlap resolution, removal order, or whitespace normalization.
atoms.title: Prompt-cleaning collision semantics are unspecified

atoms.statement: MGAC-001 is explicitly compatibility-only retired lineage and may not re-own behavior.
atoms.title: Retired source bridge is non-authoritative

atoms.statement: Capability payloads separate enabled_on_instance from usable_now and disclose blocking and evaluated identity context.
atoms.title: Capability usability is caller-specific

atoms.statement: Planning visual references name identity and provenance fields but do not define their lifecycle, access checks, retention, or invalid transitions.
atoms.title: Planning visual artifact lifecycle is under-specified

atoms.statement: Vision Bridge eligibility distinguishes native input from generated media and binds fallback to current route evidence, policy, permissions, and provider availability.
atoms.title: Vision Bridge eligibility is route-specific

atoms.statement: MultimodalInputSettlement names required concepts and acceptance examples, but the PlanUnit does not fully specify a typed wire schema, state machine, cardinality, or request-envelope integration.
atoms.title: Multimodal input settlement remains non-buildable

atoms.statement: Fallback captioning is opt-in, visible, artifact-backed, and must disclose that the selected model saw text rather than original media.
atoms.title: Fallback captioning preserves user-visible modality truth

atoms.statement: The repair addendum defines temporary persistence, cleanup events and reason codes, and the UI exit conditions for cleanup-required state.
atoms.title: Partial media artifact cleanup is concretely governed

atoms.statement: The audit-lineage note explicitly keeps the shared MGAC-100/101 schema-detail row deferred despite the repair addendum's field lists.
atoms.title: Multimodal policy schema closure is explicitly deferred

atoms.statement: Before any destructive cleanup, the contract needs canonicalization, selected-lane ownership validation, symlink handling, and an explicit refusal when the resolved repository root is not the authorized work root.
atoms.title: Destructive cleanup does not authenticate work_dir scope

atoms.statement: Broad untracked cleanup is explicitly confined to prepare_working_directory; cleanup_after_execution is forbidden from removing untracked workspace files.
atoms.title: Prepare-only broad cleanup is a clear safety invariant

atoms.statement: The plan needs a preflight/dry-run plus an explicit partial-mutation result and policy gate; best-effort continuation is not safe after an indeterminate destructive prepare.
atoms.title: Prepare errors continue after potentially partial deletion

atoms.statement: The plan simultaneously requires and forbids prepare/cleanup methods on PlatformRunner; the obsolete contract language must be retired or explicitly marked historical.
atoms.title: Runner lifecycle contract contradicts its concrete design

atoms.statement: Process identity and process-tree ownership must be returned by execution and passed to cleanup; pid 0 cannot satisfy the termination contract.
atoms.title: Cleanup termination contract is defeated by pid 0

atoms.statement: The no-secrets invariant needs a mandatory fail-closed scan boundary, structured redaction ownership, and executable tests for staged files and every evidence/log/PR sink.
atoms.title: No-secrets policy lacks a mandatory enforcement oracle

atoms.statement: Evidence pruning needs immutable lineage IDs, active-writer leases, minimum-age protection, a dry-run manifest, idempotent tombstones, and a recovery/rollback contract before retain_last_runs can be enabled.
atoms.title: Evidence pruning can delete live or misclassified evidence

atoms.statement: The fallback/default policy must be one exact value; absence or migration failure should not silently opt a project into broad untracked deletion.
atoms.title: Conservative default conflicts with git-clean-by-default

atoms.statement: Preview must be required for broad clean, ignored-file clean, all-worktree clean, and evidence pruning, with exact resolved scope and immutable deletion manifest shown before confirmation.
atoms.title: Manual destructive cleanup can confirm without exact preview

atoms.statement: Execution needs a durable lifecycle state and cancellation-safe cleanup guard, plus startup reconciliation for runs left in executing or cleanup-pending state.
atoms.title: Sequential wrapper does not guarantee cleanup on abnormal exit

atoms.statement: KeyBinding needs a versioned semantic representation and explicit per-platform display/translation rules with keyboard-layout and assistive-input tests.
atoms.title: Cross-platform shortcut mapping is underspecified

atoms.statement: Skill CRUD requires canonical path containment, symlink and special-file policy, bounded copy limits, atomic staging, collision handling, and an authorization check for project versus global roots.
atoms.title: Skill CRUD lacks a safe filesystem authority boundary

atoms.statement: Pattern resolution must define deterministic overlap precedence and default behavior, with exhaustive tests for exact, wildcard, multiple-match, case, and malformed-pattern cases.
atoms.title: Skill permission overlap can produce nondeterministic authority

atoms.statement: The import contract must fix unknown-action and collision outcomes before implementation readiness can be asserted.
atoms.title: Shortcut import remains behaviorally undecided

atoms.statement: Skill edits need content-hash compare-and-swap, atomic replace, explicit Reload/Overwrite/Cancel semantics, and recovery of unsaved editor content after a conflict.
atoms.title: Concurrent skill edits have no canonical lost-update behavior

atoms.statement: PM-native registry, permission, readiness, bundling, and skill-tool behavior are canonical; provider-native artifacts are optional projections with independently tracked state.
atoms.title: Skill runtime authority is clearly separated from projections

atoms.statement: The shortcut subsystem specifies unit and round-trip tests for its central data transformations.
atoms.title: Shortcut core has explicit unit-test oracles

atoms.statement: Destructive cleanup must acquire a scoped lease or prove exclusive package/lane/worktree ownership; if exclusivity cannot be proven, broad cleanup must refuse to run.
atoms.title: Concurrent-run cleanup race is knowingly left unsafe

atoms.statement: None must have one fail-safe meaning, represented as an explicit config state with a migration rule and observable reason.
atoms.title: Missing CleanupConfig has two opposite meanings

atoms.statement: Cross-plan reconciliation explicitly makes cleanup package-, lane-, and worktree-scoped and subordinates it to FileSafe and safe-point ownership.
atoms.title: Cross-plan cleanup authority is correctly lane-scoped
